# The common endpoint profile excludes an ordinary section-weight obstruction

The calculations below independently certify the ordinary triangle
obstruction supplied by the the contributor and explain why it cannot occur
in the proposed bad common-cap menu. They do not prove the strengthened
ordinary section-weight conjecture with the joint profile imposed.

## 1. An ordinary centroid counterexample to the cap-threshold-only claim

Let

    K=conv{(4,-3),(-3,4),(-1,-1)},
    v_1=(1,0), v_2=(0,1), v_3=(-1,-1).

The origin is the actual centroid and belongs to int K; the three
vertices sum to zero and are noncollinear. The area is k=21/2. The
normals span R^2 and sum to zero. Each positive cap isolates one
vertex. For its positive vertex height h and negative vertex heights
-r,-s, the cap's area fraction is h^2/[(h+r)(h+s)], by similarity
along the two adjacent edges. Consequently

    (q_1,q_2,q_3)/k=(16/35,16/35,4/9),
    (q_1,q_2,q_3)=(24/5,24/5,14/3).

All three fractions are strictly less than 128/279, since
16*279=4464<4480=128*35 and 4/9<16/35.

The normalized section density of such a vertex cap is 2q_i/h_i,
where h_i is measured in the unnormalized linear functional v_i.
Thus

    (sigma_1,sigma_2,sigma_3)=(12/5,12/5,14/3).

Writing lambda_i=1/sigma_i gives

    lambda_3/sum_i lambda_i=9/44<2/9,

because 81<88. Hence the proposed lower bound on inverse-section
weights is false even at a true ordinary centroid with every cap
fraction strictly below 128/279. No mixed A,B realization is claimed.

## 2. The exact profile required by one common endpoint

Suppose instead that actual A,K,B fibers admit three actual common
ambient caps with zero captured B volume, own K masses q_i, and A
masses U_i. Assume the A traces cover A. This holds in the normalized
B-support circuit with positive continuous-normal dependence, but
the following argument only needs this stated cover. Then

    U_i+q_i=Q.

For any planar convex body D of area W and any three covering closed
halfspaces with cap masses t_1<=t_2<=t_3, one has

    W<=t_3+t_2+t_1/4.                                            (1)

To prove it, remove from each of the second and third caps a distal
parallel cap of area t_i-t_1. Ordinary cap-volume continuity permits
this exactly, with null boundary lines. The retained convex body has
area at least W-t_2-t_3+2t_1, while all three original caps have retained
area at most t_1. If the retained area is positive, its centroid belongs
to a covering cap. Ordinary planar Grunbaum gives retained area at most
9t_1/4. This proves (1). If the lower bound on retained area is
nonpositive, (1) follows immediately. Zero t_1 is included by the same
argument; no positive retained convex body can have three zero-area
caps covering its centroid.

Order the OWN K cap masses as x<=y<=z and define

    F_K=x+y+z/4.

The A masses have the reverse ordering. Applying (1) to the ONE actual
A therefore gives

    a<=9Q/4-F_K.                                                (2)

If B is nonheavy, b<=a+k, and the common cap budget satisfies
Q<=(2/9)(a+b+k), then

    9Q/4<=a+k,
    F_K<=k.                                                      (3)

If the budget inequality is strict, the second inequality is strict
as well. This distinction is retained: weak premises give only the
weak conclusion. It is invalid to test small ordinary K caps while
discarding (2), because their opposite endpoint captures are required
to come from the same convex A and the same Q.

For the triangle in Section 1,

    F_K=14/3+24/5+(24/5)/4=32/3>21/2=k,
    F_K-k=1/6.

It therefore cannot occur in any common zero-B, covered-A menu
satisfying the weak proposed budget and B-nonheavy condition, regardless
of how its sections might be supplemented by A. This rules out the
specific ordinary obstruction even at equality of the target budget.

## 3. A separate actual moment cost of that ordinary triangle

The first two source cutting chords have endpoints -7/5 and 1 in
their respective tangential coordinates. Their midpoint displacement
has absolute value 1/5 and their normalized length is 12/5. The proved
actual critical-facet moment inequality says that if s_i denotes the
opposite A cutting-section density, then

    |c_(K,i)|<=s_i(sigma_i-s_i)/(sigma_i+2s_i).

Thus any such actual critical realization of those chords would have
to satisfy

    1/5<=s_i(12/5-s_i)/(12/5+2s_i),
    s_i>=1-sqrt(13)/5, i=1,2.                                  (4)

This is obtained by solving 25s_i^2-50s_i+12<=0; all denominators are
positive. It is only a necessary section cost. It is not on its own
an exclusion by a small area assumption. The actual contradiction for
this triangle is the common-profile inequality in Section 2.

The strengthened ordinary question retaining small cap fractions,
F_K<=k, and possibly the actual moment inequalities remains distinct
from the disproved cap-threshold-only statement. No triangle extremal
reduction, compactness stability margin, or universal weight bound is
asserted here.
